models.author: andrewfrueh on Sketchfab
models.note: A rod-shaped bacterium bristling with short pili, in a muted teal (E. coli has no natural color; this is an illustration convention). Its body is calibrated to the listed 2 micrometer length of E. coli. Its flagella are shortened to fit the explorer; real E. coli flagella trail several times the body length.

operations: Started from the repo's existing sketchfab-bacterium-piliated-v3.glb (no re-download)
Identified the 5 separate flagellum strands as disconnected mesh components (union-find over shared vertices) within the 'body end' hair mesh, each 3.7-5.8 model units long versus the 7.07-unit body

Scaled each flagellum toward its base-attachment point (not a crop) so every strand's extent shrinks to about 1.5 units, keeping its tapered tip intact with no open cut; the ~218 short pili strands were left untouched

This brings the full model extent (body + shortened flagella + pili) to 8.92 units, 1.26x the calibrated body length, inside the 1.3x limit; previously the full extent (13.23 units) was 1.87x, dominated by flagella extending far past the body
Removed the body's baked red/pink base-color JPEG texture (source of the 'raw meat' look) and set a flat baseColorFactor instead; kept the normal map so the membrane still has subtle bump detail
Set the pili/flagella material to a pale cream instead of its previous light-blue tint
glTF Transform 4.5.0 prune to drop the now-unused texture and accessors

models.author: Kristen Browne / NIAID, via NIH 3D Print Exchange
models.note: NIAID's SARS-CoV-2 virion model from the NIH 3D Print Exchange: a lipid envelope (teal) studded with spike trimers (gray) and membrane proteins (orange). It is an illustrative, artist-built model rather than a cryo-electron tomography reconstruction, simplified here for the web. The envelope, not counting the spikes, is calibrated to the listed 91 nm; the spikes reach about 20 nm beyond it.

operations: Download SARSCOV2_Thick_NIH3D.glb from NIH 3D (submission 17182, run 20e70d77-195b-4032-bb74-2a8c59184a43, output-file 386420)
gltf-transform weld (merge duplicate vertices)
gltf-transform simplify --ratio 0.09 --error 0.01 (566,399 -> 50,522 triangles, vertex colors preserved through decimation)
gltf-transform prune + dedup

Measured envelope vs. full extent with a custom script (measure_corona.py) that classifies vertices by COLOR_0 (teal/blue = envelope, pale = spikes, orange = HE/membrane proteins) and compares mean envelope radius to overall bounding-box extent

models.author: johnnokomis on Sketchfab
models.note: A drone photogrammetry scan of the football field at Milton Frank Stadium in Huntsville, Alabama, cropped to the playing surface; stands, track, lights, and the noisily scanned goalposts were removed. The goal-line-to-goal-line span, 100 yards (91.44 m), is calibrated to the listed length; it is about three quarters of the mesh, which also includes both end zones and a strip of turf beyond them.

operations: Rejected the user-chosen Lincoln Financial Field model (isDownloadable=false, no usable license) and the suggested search results that were mostly soccer pitches or game-asset low-poly fields; selected Milton Frank Stadium (CC-BY, isDownloadable, real photogrammetry with legible field markings) instead
Staged via scripts/sketchfab_models.py with texture-size 1024 (source has 21 mesh chunks sharing one 1024x1024 baseColor JPEG, KHR_materials_unlit)

Computed the node hierarchy's cumulative transform analytically and applied it to bake all 21 chunks into one world-space vertex soup (custom Python script using scripts/fetch_model_assets.py's GLB helpers + numpy)

Classified vertices by sampling the baseColor texture at each vertex's UV (green turf vs red track) to find the field's XZ density plateau (heatmap + 1D histograms), then kept only triangles whose 3 vertices fall inside that XZ rectangle and a tight Y-band at field level (drops stands, track, lights, parking, and the noisy goalpost geometry)
Baked a 90 degree yaw so the field's long axis (originally world Z) became world X

Repacked a single-primitive GLB, then ran glTF-Transform weld -> simplify (ratio 0.28, error 0.01) -> quantize (KHR_mesh_quantization) to go from 1,900,050 to 50,407 triangles and from 66.9 MB to 1.42 MB while preserving the flat playing surface's texture and markings
Set material doubleSided=true so the plane is not invisible if the camera dips below field level

operations: Sampled public Terrarium z12 elevation tiles around 27.9881 N, 86.9250 E using scripts/build_everest_dem.py

models.author: Mapzen Terrain Tiles / Tilezen; open-ocean bathymetry is NOAA NCEI's ETOPO1; block adaptation by Universe Scales
models.license: Mapzen Terrain Tiles attribution; underlying ETOPO1 bathymetry is U.S. public-domain NOAA data
models.note: A true-scale block of ocean around Challenger Deep, from public Mapzen elevation tiles whose open-ocean depths come from NOAA's ETOPO1 grid (about 1.85 km resolution, so the seafloor is smoothed). The deepest sample is anchored to the surveyed 10,935 m, and sea level to that point is calibrated to the listed 11,000 m; a thin rock slab sits below. The translucent blue is the water column: Everest, at 8.8 km, would fit inside it with more than 2 km to spare.

operations: Fetched the public Terrarium z10 elevation tile (about 150 m/pixel at this latitude) covering 11.3299 N, 142.1993 E with scripts/build_dem_block.py --mode sea; z11/z12 tiles in this remote area returned flat, no-data pixels and were not usable
Sampled a 91x91 grid (about 13.49 km square, step 1 native pixel) centered on the pixel nearest the 2010 CCOM/JHC multibeam sonar position for Challenger Deep

Applied one narrow Gaussian correction anchoring the sampled deepest pixel (-10,905 m) to the surveyed -10,935 m, without rescaling the rest of the sampled relief (build_everest_dem.py's summit-correction technique, generalized to a minimum instead of a maximum)

Built an opaque seafloor top surface colored by a depth-stretched bathymetric ramp, plus opaque rock walls dropping from the terrain boundary to a flat base 300 m below the deepest point and a floor cap closing the block

Added a second, translucent primitive (alphaMode BLEND, RGBA vertex colors) for the water shell: a flat quad at sea level (y=0) plus walls following the terrain boundary from y=0 down to the seafloor, colored lighter/more transparent near the top and darker/more opaque toward the bottom
Packed both primitives into one GLB buffer (scripts/fetch_model_assets.py pack_glb); no Draco, meshopt, or external textures
Added extras.label nodes at the deepest sampled point ("Challenger Deep, about 10.9 km") and at the sea-level plane ("Sea level")

models.author: Leah Hustak and Ralf Crawford (STScI) for NASA, ESA, CSA and STScI; released June 26, 2024
models.license: Public domain (NASA/STScI-produced educational material; page states no explicit license)
models.note: STScI's 3D model of the Pillars of Creation in the Eagle Nebula, built from Hubble and Webb observations, showing the four separate dust clouds that overlap as three pillars in the flat image. The tallest pillar's height is calibrated to the listed 5 light-years (the four-pillar group is about 1.2 times wider). Depth is an interpretive reconstruction, the surface is schematic, and the color is a uniform dust brown rather than an observation.

operations: Downloaded the 'All Four Pillars (Positioning Reference)' STL from the NASA Science asset page (the 3D-print base plate was not used)
Converted binary STL to GLB with pillars-helpers/stl2glb.py (welded vertices, 737,170 triangles)
Dropped disconnected fragments under 1,000 triangles; permuted axes (x,y,z)->(y,z,x) so the pillars' long axis is vertical and the four pillars spread horizontally; centered horizontally, base at y=0
gltf-transform 4.5.0 simplify --ratio 0.07 --error 0.01 (737k to 51.6k triangles)
Recomputed smooth vertex normals and assigned a dust-brown material (pillars-helpers/post.py)
gltf-transform 4.5.0 quantize
Replaced zero-length normals (degenerate triangles) with +Y

models.note: Manhattan Island drawn at true 1:1 horizontal scale from public elevation tiles and OpenStreetMap: shoreline, parks, every mapped building footprint (texture) and the roughly 1,180 buildings taller than 65 m extruded to their mapped heights. The island is turned so its long axis runs left to right (The Battery at left, Inwood at right); it is about 21 km long and 4 km wide, and the listed 21,600 m is its length. Sea level is flat, river depths are not modeled, and the neighbouring shores in the frame are only partly complete.

operations: Fetched Mapzen Terrarium z13 tiles (about 14.5 m/pixel) covering the area and bilinearly sampled a 100 m height grid rotated 22 degrees so the Battery-Inwood axis lies along +X (scripts/build_manhattan_block.py)
Fetched OSM coastline, parks/ponds and 256,792 building ways from the Overpass API; land/sea by flood-filling the rasterized coastline, neighbouring mainland recovered within ~25 m of OSM buildings
Textured the terrain block (2560 x 620 JPEG, ~8.6 m/pixel: sea, land, parks, all building footprints shaded by height); water is flat at y=0 (sea level), a rock/water skirt extends to y=-80 m
Extruded 1,183 OSM footprints with height >= 65 m (height tag or building:levels x 3.3 m), Douglas-Peucker simplified at 3 m, ear-clipped roofs, vertex-colored, flat-shaded (no normals)
Added extras.label nodes for The Battery and Inwood; no Draco/meshopt; single GLB

models.note: A terrain strip along the Panama Canal at true 1:1 horizontal scale (Atlantic and Colon at left, Pacific at right) from Mapzen/SRTM elevation, with Gatun Lake at its 26 m operating level, Miraflores Lake, the sea and the OpenStreetMap canal route drawn on it. Heights are exaggerated 8 times so the lake steps and hills are visible. The strip is about 73 km long in a straight line; the 82 km canal length is measured along its winding route, and river/lake depths are not modeled.

operations: Fetched Mapzen Terrarium z12 tiles (about 38 m/pixel) and sampled them onto a 2560 x 597 texture grid and a 250 m mesh, rotated so the Atlantic-to-Pacific chord lies along +X (scripts/build_panama_canal_block.py)
Sea = DEM cells at or below 0.6 m connected to open-sea seeds; lakes from OpenStreetMap multipolygons (Lago Gatun forced to 26 m, Lago Miraflores 16.5 m, others at their median DEM)
Heights multiplied by 8; hillshaded elevation-tint texture with sea, lake and the OSM 'Canal de Panama' centerline/lock ways drawn on it; skirt to y=-300 (drawn units)
Extras label nodes for Colon, Gatun Locks, Gatun Lake, Miraflores Locks and Panama City; no Draco/meshopt
processing.source_model_name: Mapzen Terrarium z12 tiles + OpenStreetMap extracts

coverage_gaps.note: No Jupiter volume or Moon diameter item exists in the current exports. Earth-Moon Distance is not a Moon diameter; Earth's oceans is not Earth volume. Human skin area is deliberately not matched to an uncalibrated figure.
